title: Section equivalence identifies the canonical derived open adjunction
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use small pro-étale sites small relative to the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $T=U,X$, put $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], also denoting its reconstructed section-ring sheaf by $R_T$, and let $E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ be the fixed equivalence preserving underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_j:j^{-1}R_X\cong R_U$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Write $j_{!,\mathrm{int}}\dashv j^*_{\mathrm{int}}$ for the specified internal module adjunction [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], and $j_{!,\mathrm{sec}}\dashv j^*_{\mathrm{sec}}$ for the specified section-module extension-by-zero/restriction adjunction of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. The localized site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] is identified with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by the site equivalence of Part (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization].
The canonical comparison $E_Xj_{!,\mathrm{int}}\cong j_{!,\mathrm{sec}}E_U$ identifies the scalar actions on the sheafified extension presheaves [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]: on the summand indexed by $\varphi:V\to U$, $r\in R_X(V)$ acts as $m\mapsto\alpha_j(r|_U)m$. Under this comparison and the canonical pullback comparison, the specified ordinary Hom bijections coincide, including their units and counits. Both extension and restriction are exact on both sides.
Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the induced section equivalences $D(E_T)$ and canonical pullback comparison $b:D(E_U)Lj^*_{\mathrm{int}}\cong Lj^*_{\mathrm{sec}}D(E_X)$ of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization]. Let $e_{\mathrm{int}}=D(j_{!,\mathrm{int}})$ and $e_{\mathrm{sec}}=D(j_{!,\mathrm{sec}})$ be the termwise localized extensions. Give $e_{\mathrm{int}}\dashv Lj^*_{\mathrm{int}}$ and $e_{\mathrm{sec}}\dashv Lj^*_{\mathrm{sec}}$ their independently specified adjunctions obtained by localizing the ordinary adjunctions [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], with the right adjoints expressed through the canonical exact left-derived comparisons. Localizing the ordinary extension comparison gives $c:D(E_X)e_{\mathrm{int}}\cong e_{\mathrm{sec}}D(E_U)$. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_U})$, $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X})$ on the internal side, and $q:e_{\mathrm{int}}K\to M$, their specified derived Hom bijections $h_{\mathrm{int}},h_{\mathrm{sec}}$ satisfy
$$h_{\mathrm{sec}}\bigl(D(E_X)(q)\circ c_K^{-1}\bigr)=b_M\circ D(E_U)\bigl(h_{\mathrm{int}}(q)\bigr).$$
Thus these particular comparisons identify the canonical derived open adjunctions, including their units and counits, on all unbounded complexes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pd-section-open-generator-scalar] to the fixed abelian unit and actual coefficient morphism. This proves the first scalar equation; the second follows by the linearity of each component of ordinaryExtensionComparison.

The definition of ordinaryExtensionComparison chooses the unique comparison whose mate is pullComparison. Extract this property from openComparison_existsUnique. Apply the adjunction transpose identity [lem-pur-adjunction-mate-transpose] for the ordinary Hom equation. The unit_mateEquiv and mateEquiv_counit identities, cancelling the invertible comparison when necessary, give the ordinary unit and counit equations.

Infer exactness of the internal extension and inverse image and the section extension and inverse image from their existing finite-limit and finite-colimit instances. These are the exact operations used by the fixed derived realizations, with no boundedness hypotheses.

Use the unit formula of [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] to compute the units of the independent exact localizations [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] after the standard exact-functor factors. On cochain complexes cancel the inverse factors. Pass to homotopy objects using quotientCompQhIso, then use localization extensionality to identify these adjunctions with the standard levelwise derived adjunctions. This verifies equality of the specified adjunction data, rather than replacing them by transported data.

Apply the proved source-library theorem Adjunction.mapDerivedCategoryAdjunction_mate to the ordinary comparison and its unit equation, with the two section equivalence functors as the vertical exact functors. Rewrite by Step 4. Expand the existing definition of derivedPullComparison: it is already the localized ordinary pull comparison preceded by the canonical exact left-derived comparison. In the unit of ofNatIsoRight the inverse comparison cancels that factor. Cancel the inverse extension comparison to obtain the displayed derived unit equation.

source.place: Adjunction.mapDerivedCategoryAdjunction_mate; the source lemma is proved, and its fixed adjunctions are identified with the independent exact localizations in Step 4.

proof.text: The derived unit equation determines the mate of the inverse extension comparison: apply the inverse mate equivalence and the injective section Hom bijection to its components, then cancel the extension comparison. Use [lem-pur-adjunction-mate-transpose] for every derived morphism to obtain the Hom equation. Apply mateEquiv_counit to obtain the final derived counit equation. Assemble these equations, the eight exactness instances, and the two scalar identities into the unchanged conjunction.
